speaker_role: independent counselor/consultancy marketer (podcast host, former admissions counselor/college counselor, launching own consulting business)
commercial_incentive: Explicitly announces and promotes a new paid college consulting business ('Avila College Consulting') with a discounted beta program and free 20-minute consultation offer
key_insights: Speaker describes being first-generation and not knowing about selective-enrollment high school options, which limited her own college search to schools without essay requirements and with low test-score thresholds
Argues first-generation parents (not just first-gen students) are underserved because even if the parents attended college, admissions norms have changed since their own experience

Notes a gap she observed while reviewing applications: students who are technically not 'first-gen' but whose families lack longstanding higher-ed experience often write less polished essays and may apply to schools that are not a good fit
Describes her own path: transferred colleges after freshman year to get a fuller on-campus experience and to rejoin an activity (orchestra) not offered at her first, commuter-only school
Frames financial aid trade-offs concretely: living on campus vs. commuting changed her own aid package and out-of-pocket cost
Advocates working with independent educational consultants (IECs)/college counseling consultants as a way to level the playing field for first-gen and under-resourced families
States there are over 4,000 colleges and universities in the US, implying families shouldn't limit themselves only to schools they've already heard of
specific_numbers_or_facts: Speaker states there are over 4,000 colleges and universities in the United States
notable_or_distinctive: A personal, first-person narrative from a former admissions/college counseling professional reflecting on her own first-generation college search mistakes, framed specifically around underserved first-gen Latina families, rather than generic application advice.
reliability_notes: This is a personal biography/business-launch podcast episode, not a structured how-to guide; most of the runtime is autobiographical narrative and a sales pitch for her new consulting practice rather than actionable, generalizable admissions guidance.
